deep.reconstruction:
Setting. M is a small category of 'models' sitting inside its presheaf category \hat M by Yoneda, so M ⊂ \hat M. The previous page suggests the models are combinatorial cells: a family of posets J_n (the I_n^* of p.11), each with a top element d_n, a rank function τ_n, and the property that each lower interval (J_n)_{≤η} is again some J_{n'}. These are regular-polytope-like face posets, and Grothendieck asks whether there are examples other than I_n^* ("Ça doit être dans les livres de Coxeter!").

Definition of B_0. B_0 is the full subcategory of \hat M of presheaves X such that:
(i) X is the sup (union) of its subobjects isomorphic to models, i.e. X is covered by monic cells S ↪ X with S in M. The margin notes the consequence that every section ξ of X lies in the image of some mono S → X with S in M.
(ii) For two model subobjects K, L ⊂ X, the intersection K ∩ L is again the union of the model subobjects it contains.
This is a 'non-singular / regular' cell-complex condition, the analogue for general M of non-singular simplicial sets or regular CW complexes.

The pinned poset. Next one takes the set of model subobjects of X, ordered by inclusion. A correction in the image replaces this X̃ by an abstract K. Such a poset carries an 'M-épinglage' (M-pinning):
(a) a strictly increasing 'length' function τ_K : K → ℕ;
(b) for each ξ in K with n = τ_K(ξ), an isomorphism u^K_ξ : J_n ≅ K_{≤ξ} with u^K_ξ(d_n) = ξ.
The maps J_n → K so obtained (one for each ξ in K(n) = τ^{-1}(n)) are called 'admissible'.

Axioms on the next page.
(1) τ_K ∘ u^K_ξ = τ_n.
(2) Transitivity: u^K_ξ ∘ u^n_η = u^K_{u^K_ξ(η)}.

Claims on p.13.
- The groupoid of admissible objects of \hat M (with isomorphisms) is equivalent to the groupoid of M-pinned posets.
- Morphisms between such objects can also be reconstructed. They are the strictly increasing maps f : K → L that preserve τ and make the restrictions K_{≤ξ} → L_{≤f(ξ)} commute with the pinnings by J_n.
In other words, the dimension-preserving, cellwise-injective maps.

Purpose. This is a combinatorial description of 'regular' presheaves on a test or shape category by posets with characteristic-map data. It serves to model homotopy types (Champs / Pursuing Stacks context) by polyhedral posets, generalizing the simplicial case to other regular-polytope families of models.
errors: The equivalence with pinned posets tacitly needs hypotheses on M that are not stated here. Model subobjects of a model J_n must correspond exactly to elements of J_n (faces), and monos between models must be determined by their underlying poset maps. Automorphisms of models must also be accounted for: the pinning is extra data, so different choices give isomorphic pinned posets. Without this, the functor X ↦ (poset of model subobjects) need not be fully faithful.

Strict increase of τ_K together with τ_K∘u_ξ = τ_n forces rank-compatibility, but τ is only claimed strictly increasing, not a grading. Whether every pinned poset is realized by an object of B_0 (essential surjectivity) is asserted on the next page without proof.
Condition (ii) is stated only for pairs of model subobjects. That suffices for presheaf unions, but it must be checked to give that the poset of model subobjects determines X.

ideas.what: Subcategory of presheaves on a category of cell-models that are unions of monic cells with 'regular' intersections (non-singular presheaves)
ideas.modern_name: non-singular / regular simplicial (or M-)sets; regular presheaves on Eilenberg–Zilber or skeletal categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: Non-singular simplicial sets: Waldhausen–Jahren–Rognes (2013), Fjellbo; regular presheaves in test-category theory: Cisinski (2006)
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks discusses related ordered-set models of homotopy types; this exact definition is unsure

ideas.what: Encoding such presheaves by posets with a rank function and chosen isomorphisms J_n ≅ K_{≤ξ} satisfying transitivity ('M-épinglage')
ideas.modern_name: CW posets / face posets of regular CW complexes; simplicial posets (Stanley) with characteristic-map data

ideas.what: Morphisms reconstructed as rank-preserving increasing maps compatible with the pinnings
ideas.modern_name: cellular (dimension-preserving, cellwise injective) maps of regular complexes

missed.claim: A general framework: for any family of 'regular' cell-models J_n whose lower intervals are again models (regular-polytope-like, possibly beyond simplices and cubes), regular presheaves on M are equivalent to M-pinned posets. Grothendieck wanted to combine this with the search on p.11 for other flag-transitive model families. This parametrizes a whole class of shape categories by sequences of regular polytopes, a uniform treatment the literature does piecemeal (simplicial posets, cubical posets, CW posets).
missed.quote: Alors $\tilde{X}$ est un ens ordonné, muni de la structure ("M-épinglage de $K$")
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Could give a uniform combinatorial model for non-singular presheaves on test categories of polytopal shapes. This is relevant to Cisinski-style homotopy theory and to poset models of homotopy types. Mostly anticipated by Björner and Stanley in special cases.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, general pinned-poset description of regular presheaves on arbitrary polytopal model categories, linked to the Coxeter-regularity question of the previous page. The individual ideas (CW posets, simplicial posets, non-singular simplicial sets) are known in special cases, so this is a modestly interesting unpublished generalization, not a surprise.
transcription_corrections: 'Soit Donc $\tilde{X}$ l'un des sous-objets' should probably read 'Soit donc $\tilde X$ l'ensemble des sous-objets de X qui sont des modèles'; the corrected letter K is written above.

'Une application strictement croissante $K \xrightarrow{\tau_K} \mathbb{N}$ (application "longueur")': the arrow target is ℕ, and the parenthetical reads roughly 'application "longueur"' or 'dimension'.
Margin: 'cela implique que ∀ ξ ∈ X, il existe un S → X, S ∈ M, mono' — the barred S is just S.
Bottom left: 'les applications $J_n \to K$ définies par les $\xi \in K(n) = \tau^{-1}(n)$ sont dites admissibles'.
